lessons.title: Daily care of chickens in the house
lessons.html:
Your work in the chicken house

On a poultry farm you look after living animals. Chickens need water, feed, fresh air, the right temperature and a clean, dry floor every day. If one of these is missing, the birds get sick or die. Your work is very important.

Water

  • Check that every drinker or nipple line gives water.
  • Clean drinkers when they are dirty.
  • Set the height of the drinkers to the size of the birds, as your supervisor shows you.
  • Tell your supervisor at once if water stops.

Feed

  • Check that feeders are full but not overflowing.
  • Make sure the feed line motor is running.
  • Do not waste feed. Spilled feed brings rats.
  • Use the feed type your supervisor tells you, for example starter, grower or layer feed.

Air and temperature

Watch the birds. If they crowd together under the heater, they are cold. If they pant with open beaks and hold their wings out, they are hot. Tell your supervisor. Check that fans run and curtains are set as you were told.

Litter

Litter is the wood shavings or other bedding on the floor. It must stay dry. Wet litter makes ammonia, a strong smell that hurts the birds' eyes and lungs. Fix leaking drinkers and turn or replace wet patches as your supervisor shows you.

Eggs

On a layer or breeder farm you collect eggs at set times each day. Handle eggs gently. Put cracked and dirty eggs aside. Count the eggs and write the number down.

Writing things down

Each day, write on the house sheet: dead birds, feed, water meter reading and temperature. Your supervisor uses this to see if the flock is doing well.

lessons.title: Keeping chickens healthy and keeping disease out
lessons.html:
Signs of a sick bird

A healthy chicken is alert, moves well, eats and drinks. A sick chicken may:

  • sit alone with ruffled feathers and closed eyes
  • not eat or drink
  • have runny droppings, or blood in the droppings
  • cough, sneeze or breathe with a rattling sound
  • have a swollen head or a blue comb
  • walk badly or lie down

If you see sick birds, or more dead birds than normal, tell your supervisor straight away. Do not wait until the end of the day.

Dead birds

Pick up dead birds every day. Wear gloves. Count them and write the number down. Put them where the farm says, such as the incinerator or the disposal pit. Never give dead birds to people or dogs, and never leave them lying around.

Vaccines and medicine

Your supervisor or the vet decides on vaccines and medicine. You may help give them in the water or by spray. Follow the instructions exactly. Wash your hands after. Never give medicine on your own.

Biosecurity: keep germs out

Germs can come onto the farm on people, shoes, clothes, vehicles, wild birds and rats. To keep them out:

  1. Sign the register at the gate.
  2. Shower or wash your hands and change into farm clothes and boots.
  3. Step into the footbath at every house door.
  4. Do not go from a sick house to a healthy house. Work in the young or healthy birds first.
  5. Do not keep your own chickens at home if the farm rule says no. Home chickens can carry disease.
  6. Close doors and report holes in the mesh.
  7. Do not bring food into the chicken house.

Your own safety

Wear a dust mask in dusty houses. Wear gloves for dead birds and chemicals. Wash your hands before you eat.

Key points

  • Chickens need water, feed, fresh air, the right heat and dry litter every day.
  • Tell your supervisor at once about sick or extra dead birds.
  • Pick up dead birds daily with gloves and dispose of them the farm's way.
  • Use the footbath and change clothes before entering a house.
  • Never give medicine without instructions from your supervisor or vet.
